title: Wireshark? Add ability to display protocol field values
description:
In most cases Wireskark can be somehow like Wikipedia for protocols.
Because it shows protocols fields details. Add another level and show current
value and all other possible for specific field if available.
Feature for Qt Shark.

For example: ip.proto, for example 0x11 is UDP, but which is TCP? Now you can
read it in Wireshark GUI.

![fv_where_is_menu_to_show_field_values](/uploads/47fd7d00d34ac4e66123fb876b065609/fv_where_is_menu_to_show_field_values.png)
![fv_ip_proto](/uploads/76ae9190912d99dc409f5a1194e259f2/fv_ip_proto.png)
![fv_dns](/uploads/b3622ef3d92271201fe566a8159aee7e/fv_dns.png)
![fv_range](/uploads/43f9a3eafbed0a3d66adcd738b05951e/fv_range.png)

notes.body: changed the description
marked this merge request as **ready**

Just for clarification. Does this display all possible values on a specific field (in which case it will not show you if and how a field value leads to a dissector being called) or should it display all sub dissector connections for a specific field. The ip.proto example is misleading I think, as this is actually defined via RFC. Would udp.Port and possible values for that make more sense?
@geraldcombs What do you think about this license? No problem to change to something more restrict (GPL) :smile:

It would be the first inside the UI source code (we do have a few BSD-[1,2,3]-Clause, none 0BSD yet).

Not sure on how this works out with Qt, might be, that it has to be the same license due to the Qt license restrictions

I think it would be OK to add the BSD Zero Clause license to the allowed license list. We already allow the 1-, 2-, and 3-Clause licenses and according to

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BSD_licenses#0-clause_license_(%22BSD_Zero_Clause_License%22)

it's compatible with our main license (GPL-2.0-or-later).
Done? See reply for João comment for my point of view.

I would like to bring another perspective to this. License proliferation is detrimental, and if we have to maintain this code, collectively, and we can choose the license, then I would prefer to use GPL (IOW I would probably not work on a 100% BSD Wireshark).

As I know 0BSD is the "latest" possible license, because it is simple "do everything you want" (including re-licensing to everything you want: for example commercial). It is the best license for stupid simple code, like this window is (on the other side: in my opinion you have something valuable you probably choose GPL/other to protect it)

I agree with your logic but not the way it is applied here.

This is part of a larger body of work whose default license is GPL so there should be a strong reason to deviate IMO. The conversation tends to focus exclusively on compatibility with GPL. I don't have a fundamental objection to BSD/MIT, sometimes it can be a good license, but my personal goal is not to create code as unrestricted as possible.
changed the description

Hi guys,
I really like this change, I think this could be very handy when analyzing a packet. Some considerations:

1. despite I don't have any particolar issue with a specific license, I agree with @jvalverde that having too many is bad. In some unpredictable situations, licences in conflict could bring to a dead end.
1. I agree with @rknall that the `ip.proto` example is misleading. I would take another one as main reference, and the easy proposal would be `dns.qry.type`. I would stick with this one, changing the code everywhere accordingly
1. the commits should be reworked to remove the merge commits of master over this branch.

One more thing I noticed. If you, for example, call this dialog for ip.ttl for example, the information really does not give you anything. I wonder if it should be only available for specific types, all types does not make much sense for me?

For ip.ttl basically it says "0x00-0xff: data" as information. What does that mean for the enduser? I mean, I will get it, but a generic user will not. And it will only increase confusion. 

I like the feature in general though.

That's even more confusing when selecting a string. I choose `dns.qry.name` and the window showed me value first => 0x00, value last => 2**256-1, that is totally meaningless for a string.

One more: when choosing an integer, the values should show the whole length always. Es. in `dns.qry.type` (2 bytes) it shows 0x01 and  0x1000, while I'd prefer 0x0010 and 0x1000.

ip.ttl - yes information is relatively less important but it is a consequence of bitmask. If you have a bitmask information here can be more valuable (specific case: non-continues bitmask, like 0b00110010). Instead of not displaying dialog for full mask I think better to show it in all cases.  Check: ip.frag_offset

@crondaemon 
> 0x01 and 0x1000, while I'd prefer 0x0010 and 0x1000.

0x01 is not 0x0010. Did you mean 0x0001? I decided to 0-fill to even only to improve readability. See 0x00..00.. is totally unreadable - we do not have all possible values, so better to see 0x11,0x12 0x13,0x15,0x16,0x17...
instead 0x0011,0x0012 0x0013,0x0015,0x016,0x0017

One column for:
if FT_STRING: Description: 8-bytes non-null-terminated-string?
if FT_BYTES: Description: 6-bytes?
What do you think?

Future: 
description can be improved for some details like charset/coding (for example: UTF-8 string(z))

>> I agree with @rknall that the `ip.proto` example is misleading

> Could you tell me why it is misleading? I attach image with it, I do not see > any difference comparing to dns.qry.type

It is misleading as such, as it is confusing information. The dialog is called Field Value, and is supposed to explain (at least that would be the initial assumption by many) the meaning of the value for the field. You even mention that as such, by calling Wireshark a Wiki for protocol information. I would - instead of the table - rather expect an entry per field, as it is done one https://www.wireshark.org/docs/dfref/i/ip.html for example. For fields which have entries (such as the mentioned dns.qry.type) a list of possible values could be added. But for all others, I (in the role of an unexpected user) would much rather expect an explanation, instead of a generic "0x00-0xFF: data" information which tells me nothing at all. At least the description, and a type information (here unsigned int) would make more sense to me.
When Wireshark Gitlab Utility performs a rebase, the squash with Gitlab GUI is lost and all commits appear in the Git history.

> 0x01 is not 0x0010. Did you mean 0x0001?

Yes.

> Could you tell me why it is misleading?

I tried to put myself in Average User's shoes. I can really get there are no differences between ip.proto and dns.qry.type, but ip.proto is a lower level field, while dns.qry.type is higher: I would just use the latter as reference example.

> One column for: if FT_STRING: Description: 8-bytes non-null-terminated-string? if FT_BYTES: Description: 6-bytes? What do you think?

It makes sense to me.

@crondaemon It should be done. Please review my solution.

@pquantin Are there any benefits from "Wireshark Gitlab Utility"? It is much easier to follow gitlab feature-branch way and use gitlab squash if someone needs. I hope I can work with many commits and after review do manual squash to make "ws utility" happy.

![image](/uploads/3346a60bd88ee233ffd2e18c5e91643f/image.png)

This makes even less sense for me. First, I would expect both columns for the values to have the same number of leading zeros. In that case, the first column should read 0x0000. Title should not be "Value first/last" it should rather be "Range min/max", as it is the possible range. Also, see below, the entries here are decimal, but the range is presented as hexadecimal. Not something someone would expect. 

Instead of writing "type is uint16" would it not make more sense to have a dedicated column for the type? Description for this field (dns.count.queries) would be "Number of queries in packet.

```
    { &hf_dns_count_questions,
      { "Questions", "dns.count.queries",
        FT_UINT16, BASE_DEC, NULL, 0x0,
        "Number of queries in packet", HFILL }},
```

I would also present the name for the field.

But again, UI-wise, the dialog does not make sense to me still. It is a great dialog for a field which has an enumeration based type underneath. It makes absolut no sense for the majority of fields, as you waste a lot of real-estate on screen for very little information.

Please address those issues, the dialog as such would be a great addition, but it is still WIP in my opinion

Wireshark Gitlab Utility must be used: it is the tool we use to ensure proper linear history and automatic rebasing to avoid the conflicts between multiple merge requests triggered at the same time by different reviewers. So please perform the squash manually before the merge.

We should avoid setting stuff like colors static, as it will interfere with Darkmode settings. Also, we have a generic method for selecting fonts, please use that. Otherwise if the user selected a specific monospace font his choice will not be recognized

We use

    QColor hover_color = ColorUtils::alphaBlend(palette().window(), palette().highlight(), 0.5);

in the welcome page, packet list, and packet detail. We should probably move that to a common routine in ColorUtils and use the common routine here as well. As Roland points out, you need to take dark mode into account as well, for example using `palette(text)` instead of `color:black`:

```
    hover_style = QString(
        "QTreeView:item:hover {"
        "  background-color: %1;"
        "  color: palette(text);"
        "}").arg(hover_color.name(QColor::HexArgb));
```

You can get the application-wide monospace font with `wsApp->monospaceFont()`.

> We should probably move that to a common routine in ColorUtils

Inbound in !5700.
Done

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/5685/diffs?diff_id=304987597&start_sha=cf178e3e706852dade0c51d5d2a648d3d68307f4#c2cfaf4b8a677168e5de21abfcb944660918308e_183_183)

Can you set this to `false`? I know that [lots of people like them](https://ux.stackexchange.com/questions/3562/to-use-or-not-to-use-zebra-stripes-or-alternating-row-colors-for-tables), but in our case we have two heavily-used views (the packet list and detail) that color rows in order to convey information. I'm not sure it makes sense to color rows in other widgets without conveying any information.

`alternatingRowColors` I use it to improve readability in "presentation mode" (for example meeting). If you see "white" block of many rows you probably spend more time to find values for your row. Because above and below are also white so you have a problem to locate proper row line; alternatingRowColors is in this case better then table border. I already used it in two Wireshark dialogs: Bluetooth Device and Bluetooth HCI Summary.

All "tables for data"  should have this option enabled or there should be option to enable it. So I can disable it now.

commits_data.title: WikiShark? Add ability to display protocol field values
commits_data.message:
WikiShark? Add ability to display protocol field values
